articles.title: Usina Viva promove mês de atividades culturais gratuitas em Friburgo | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto Usina Viva promove atrações ao longo de novembro; abertura será com espetáculo infantil sobre ancestralidade e cultura afro-brasileira.
articles.summary: Projeto Usina Viva promove atrações ao longo de novembro; abertura será com espetáculo infantil sobre ancestralidade e cultura afro-brasileira.
articles.body:
Usina Cultural recebe programação gratuita com teatro, música e dança em Nova Friburgo. — Foto: Divulgação

A Usina Cultural, em Nova Friburgo, na Região Serrana do Rio, tem apresentações confirmadas para os dias 7 e 19 de novembro, com programação gratuita de teatro, música e dança no Teatro da Usina Cultural.

As atividades fazem parte do projeto Usina Viva e incluem espetáculos que abordam temas como ancestralidade, cultura afro-brasileira, diversidade e expressão artística.

A montagem mistura dança, teatro e música para celebrar a cultura hip-hop e discutir temas como identidade, pertencimento, preconceito e transformação social. Com trilha sonora autoral produzida por artistas friburguenses, o espetáculo apresenta a dança como forma de expressão, acolhimento e valorização da diversidade de corpos e trajetórias.

A primeira atração será no sábado, dia 7 de novembro, às 16h, com o espetáculo infantil Travessias da Filha do Ganga por Pindorama. Na apresentação, o público acompanha a história de Ayô, filha do líder de um quilombo, em uma jornada por Pindorama. Guiada por um professor-griô, a personagem percorre um território onde passado, presente e futuro se conectam.

A obra também aborda diferentes formas de viver e se relacionar com o meio ambiente, além de destacar a ancestralidade e os saberes tradicionais. A classificação indicativa é livre.

Já no dia 19 de novembro, às 19h, o espaço recebe uma nova edição do projeto musical Luminosa, com apresentação do cantor, compositor e violonista Alexandre Carvalho, conhecido artisticamente como Alè.

O trabalho do artista reúne referências da espiritualidade afro-brasileira, da memória histórica do povo negro e da resistência cultural. Suas composições combinam pesquisa histórica e ritmos de matriz afro-brasileira. Entre os trabalhos lançados está o EP "IGBÀ", de 2025, que reúne referências às culturas afro-diaspóricas, afro-indígenas e afro-quilombolas.

A programação continua no dia 20 de novembro, às 19h, feriado do Dia da Consciência Negra, com o espetáculo "SHP – A Forma Original da Cultura".

articles.title: Governador eleito anuncia advogado para comandar Infraestrutura de RR | G1
articles.standfirst: Arthur Henrique escolheu Felikis Menezes para comandar a secretaria responsável pelas obras e pela infraestrutura em todo o estado. A indicação foi anunciada durante o processo de transição.
articles.summary: Arthur Henrique escolheu Felikis Menezes para comandar a secretaria responsável pelas obras e pela infraestrutura em todo o estado.
articles.body:
O governador eleito de Roraima, Arthur Henrique (PL) e Felipe de Souza Menezes — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

O governador eleito de Roraima, Arthur Henrique (PL) , anunciou o colega de partido e advogado Felipe de Souza Menezes , conhecido como Felikis Menezes, como futuro secretário estadual de Infraestrutura . A indicação foi divulgada nesta quinta-feira (5), por meio de uma publicação nas redes sociais.

O anúncio ocorre após o início do processo de transição entre a atual gestão , comandada pelo governador interino Soldado Sampaio (Republicanos) , e a equipe do governador eleito. Nas Eleições de 2026, Arthur recebeu 69,13% dos votos válidos no primeiro turno.

Ao anunciar a escolha, Arthur afirmou que o objetivo é preparar Roraima para ampliar a exportação de alimentos.

"Nos próximos quatro anos, Roraima vai ter a oportunidade de viver o maior salto econômico da sua história. Essa é a previsão para a conclusão do asfaltamento da estrada até Georgetown. Lá na Guiana está sendo construído um porto que vai nos conectar aos maiores mercados consumidores do planeta", afirmou.

Nas redes sociais, Felikis se apresenta como advogado e natural de Roraima. Ele disputou uma vaga na Assembleia Legislativa nas eleições de 2026, recebeu 5.908 votos e ficou como suplente.

Durante a campanha, contou com a participação frequente de Arthur Henrique, que apareceu ao lado dele em publicações e atividades eleitorais.

Arthur Henrique escolheu Felikis Menezes para comandar a secretaria responsável pelas obras e pela infraestrutura em todo o estado — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Na administração municipal de Boa Vista , ele ocupou os cargos de secretário municipal de Obras e de Segurança e Trânsito .

Durante a campanha, Arthur apresentou propostas para a recuperação de estradas vicinais, a construção de pontes e o asfaltamento da ligação rodoviária entre Roraima e Georgetown, capital da Guiana.

"Vamos industrializar, agregando valor àquilo que a gente produz aqui, gerando emprego e renda para o nosso povo. E a base para que tudo isso aconteça é infraestrutura. É estrada boa e ponte segura para escoar a produção", declarou.

Felikis agradeceu a indicação e afirmou que entre as primeiras medidas, está o levantamento das condições das vias e pontes em todas as regiões de Roraima.

"Vamos cuidar de todas as obras do nosso estado. Já recebi a missão de priorizar a infraestrutura das nossas estradas. Vamos fazer um levantamento de todas as estradas e todas as pontes de todas as regiões do nosso estado, onde há maior concentração de produção.Vamos substituir madeira por concreto onde for necessário e, assim, vamos seguir em frente", afirmou.

Em reunião realizada em 15 de outubro, no Palácio Senador Hélio Campos, em Boa Vista, Sampaio autorizou o compartilhamento de relatórios e informações administrativas e financeiras do governo estadual com a equipe do governador eleito. O encontro teve a mediação do presidente do Tribunal de Contas de Roraima (TCE-RR), conselheiro Brito Bezerra.

Na ocasião, Arthur afirmou que o objetivo é conhecer a situação da administração estadual e garantir a continuidade dos serviços essenciais a partir de janeiro.

"Meu foco não é questionar o que foi feito, mas olhar para frente e garantir que, a partir de janeiro, os serviços essenciais continuem funcionando. Para isso, precisamos conhecer os dados, trabalhar em parceria e construir uma transição responsável", afirmou.

As equipes também devem realizar visitas técnicas às secretarias e levantar informações sobre convênios, emendas parlamentares e recursos federais em tramitação.

articles.title: Why are wealthy countries failing developing nations?
articles.summary: UN report warns climate adaptation funding is falling far short of needs.
articles.body:
The United Nations Environment Programme has published a report warning that the world is not adapting quickly enough to keep pace with the growing human and economic costs linked to the climate crisis.

The UN singles out wealthy countries – responsible for the bulk of carbon emissions – for failing to meet their financial pledges.

At successive Conference of the Parties (COP) meetings, billions of dollars have been earmarked to help developing nations become more resilient.

But only a fraction has been paid out. What are the consequences?

Avantika Goswami – Climate change and green economy programme manager at the Centre for Science and Environment

Danny Sriskandarajah – Chief executive of the New Economics Foundation

articles.title: Apicultor vende produtos à base de mel há mais de 20 anos na Expoferr e define lucro como '13º salário' | G1
articles.standfirst: Anderson de Freitas vende mel em bisnaga e em favo, própolis, pólen, geleia real, cera de abelha, molho de pimenta e hidromel, uma bebida alcoólica produzida a partir da fermentação natural do mel.
articles.summary: Anderson de Freitas vende mel em bisnaga e em favo, própolis, pólen, geleia real, cera de abelha, molho de pimenta e hidromel, uma bebida alcoólica produzida a partir da fermentação natural do mel.
articles.body:
Apicultor Anderson Pereira de Freitas — Foto: Tiago Côrtes/ g1RR

"É gratificante levar o legado do meu pai" . É o que resume o apicultor Anderson Pereira de Freitas, que há 20 anos vende produtos à base de mel durante a Exposição-Feira Agropecuária de Roraima (Expoferr). Ele afirma que com as vendas feitas durante a festa garante a ele um " 13º salário ".

A feira agro, considerada a maior do setor no estado, ocorre até o próximo sábado (7) no Parque de Exposições Dandãezinho, na região do Monte Cristo, zona rural de Boa Vista .

🍯 Entre os produtos oferecidos por ele estão mel em bisnaga e em favo , própolis , pólen , geleia real , cera de abelha e molho de pimenta feito com mel . Mas, um dos destaques mesmo é o hidromel , bebida alcoólica produzida a partir da fermentação natural do mel com água.

🐝A apicultura é a atividade de criação e manejo de abelhas em colmeias com o objetivo de produzir e comercializar produtos como mel, própolis, pólen, cera e geleia real. O trabalho envolve a instalação e manutenção das colmeias, o acompanhamento dos enxames e a coleta da produção das abelhas.

Anderson é dono do apiário Freitas. Ele conta que aprendeu o trabalho com o pai, já falecido, e continua o ensinamento passado pelas gerações da família.

"Há mais de 20 anos a gente participa da Expoferr. Meu pai sempre dizia que é o nosso 13º salário. Ele não está mais comigo, mas deixou o legado dele e eu estou continuando. Já tem meu filho, que me acompanha lá no apiário. Tem seis anos, mas já me acompanha", afirmou.

🍾 A fabricação do hidromel da família Freitas é feita em parceria com o apiário Recanto da Abelha, sem conservantes ou compostos químicos. De acordo com Anderson, o processo leva entre 90 e 120 dias e exige monitoramento constante para garantir a qualidade da bebida.

Apesar dos desafios da profissão, como a necessidade de conquistar a confiança dos consumidores em relação à pureza dos produtos, o apicultor afirma que a satisfação de manter vivo o legado da família compensa as dificuldades.

"É uma profissão difícil, não é fácil. Você vende mel, muitas pessoas desconfiam, pergunto se é mel puro... Então dá muito trabalho, mas é gratificante, é gratificante levar o legado do meu pai", contou.

Este ano, a Expoferr reúne ao menos 300 empresas expositoras e deve movimentar quase R$ 1 bilhão em negócios , segundo estimativa do governo, responsável pela festa. O estado informou que investiu R$ 10 milhões em recursos estaduais para a realização do evento. A expectativa é receber 900 mil visitantes durante os cinco dias de festa.

articles.title: Cátia de França recebe título de Doutora Honoris Causa da UFPB | G1
articles.standfirst: Cerimônia de entrega de título para Cátia de França aconteceu no fim da tarde desta quinta-feira (5), na UFPB. Título é uma honraria da universidade para profissionais com trajetórias marcadas por contribuições sociais e artísticas.
articles.summary: Cerimônia de entrega de título para Cátia de França aconteceu no fim da tarde desta quinta-feira (5), na UFPB. Título é uma honraria da universidade para profissionais com trajetórias marcadas por contribuições sociais e artísticas.
articles.body:
A cantora e compositora Cátia de França recebeu o título de Doutora Honoris Causa em cerimônia realizada nesta quinta-feira (5), na Universidade Federal da Paraíba (UFPB), em João Pessoa. A homenagem reconhece a contribuição da artista para a cultura paraibana e nordestina e sua produção em diferentes áreas do conhecimento.

Durante a cerimônia de outorga do título, Cátia de França foi ovacionada pelo público presente na Sala de Concertos Radegundes Feitosa, do Centro de Comunicação, Turismo e Artes (CCTA). Participou da cerimônia a reitora da instituição, Terezinha Domiciano.

Para outorgar a homenagem, a UFPB considerou que a obra de Cátia de França dialoga com áreas acadêmicas como Música, Letras, Comunicação e Educação . A proposta foi apresentada por Bernardina Freire, responsável pela Pró-Reitoria de Extensão (Proex), e por Alexandre Santos, coordenador de Extensão Cultural da universidade.

"É maravilhoso porque na minha terra, cheguei, e voltei, 17 anos de Rio de Janeiro, e me espanto com o avanço da cidade. Então, estou assim sensibilizadíssima porque esse é o motivo de agradecer a Deus, porque acima de tudo isso aconteceu porque ele quis", disse Cátia após ganhar o título.

A reitora Terezinha Domiciano também destacou a importância da concessão do título para Cátia de França. Ela destacou a trajetória da cantora e compositora.

"O reconhecimento da universidade que dá realmente o seu maior título de homenagem a uma cidadã paraibana, negra, mulher, que teve toda uma trajetória difícil, mas mesmo assim conseguiu deixar o seu legado para a música popular brasileira, paraibana, o resgate do pertencimento de ser cidadã paraibana", ressaltou.

Cátia de França recebe título de Doutora Honoris Causa da UFPB, em cerimônia que foi realizada nesta quinta-feira (5) — Foto: Hebert Araújo/TV Cabo Branco

Cátia de França nasceu em João Pessoa, em 1947, e tem mais de cinco décadas de carreira. Sua produção musical reúne referências de ritmos como coco, ciranda, maracatu e aboio, além de elementos de gêneros como rock, jazz, blues e samba.

A artista também incorpora referências da literatura em suas músicas. Algumas de suas composições fazem referência a escritores como João Cabral de Melo Neto e José Lins do Rego.

Em 2024, Cátia lançou o álbum mais recente, “No Rastro de Catarina”, gravado ao vivo em João Pessoa e influenciado por músicos paraibanos.

Cátia de França também acumula outros reconhecimentos pela trajetória artística. Em 2024, recebeu o título de Mestre das Artes da Paraíba. No mesmo ano, sua obra foi reconhecida como Patrimônio Imaterial do Estado, e o álbum “No Rastro de Catarina” foi indicado ao Grammy Latino.

Em 2025, a artista recebeu o prêmio de Artista do Ano no 8º Prêmio Profissionais da Música.

articles.title: Crise no Paraguai: Senado começa a analisar impeachment contra o presidente Santiago Peña | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente apresentou renúncia após quebra do banco ueno, que deixou milhões de clientes sem acesso a depósitos; deputados aprovaram acusação contra Peña por suspeita de conflito de interesses.
articles.summary: Presidente apresentou renúncia após quebra do banco ueno, que deixou milhões de clientes sem acesso a depósitos; deputados aprovaram acusação contra Peña por suspeita de conflito de interesses.
articles.body:
O Senado do Paraguai retomou a sessão nesta quinta-feira (5) para analisar o processo de impeachment contra o presidente Santiago Peña . O país vive uma profunda crise política após vir a tona um escândalo envolvendo a quebra do banco ueno, que deixou milhões de clientes sem acesso a seus depósitos.

A sessão extraordinária foi aberta às 19h50 e constituída formalmente como tribunal para conduzir o processo de impeachment.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, os parlamentares designados como responsáveis pela acusação detalhavam os principais pontos da denúncia no plenário.

Os parlamentares decidiram que Santiago Peña deverá comparecer para exercer seu direito de defesa nesta sexta-feira (6), a partir das 10h.

Enquanto isso, do lado de fora do Congresso, manifestantes estão em vigília, acompanhando o julgamento político.

Veja, abaixo, a cronologia da crise no país vizinho:

Na manhã desta quinta (5), o Congresso do Paraguai deu os primeiros passos para votar um impeachment contra Santiago Peña , e contra seu vice, Pedro Alliana;

Horas depois, Peña apresentou uma carta de renúncia ;

A Câmara do Paraguai , no entanto, não aceitou a renúncia e decidiu dar seguimento do processo de impeachment contra Peña - a votação foi unânime;

Já o processo de impeachment contra o vice, Pedro Alliana, foi rejeitado . A decisão abriu caminho para Alliana assumir a presidência do país.

Durante a tarde, o Senado abriu uma sessão para julgar o pedido de renúncia do presidente Peña, mas a sessão foi suspensa por falta de quórum.

Às 19h50, o Senado abriu uma sessão extraordinária para julgar o processo de impeachment contra o presidente.

Peña vai apresentar sua defesa no processo do impeachment nesta sexta (6), às 10h.

No início da tarde, a Câmara dos Deputados aprovou por unanimidade, com 78 votos, a abertura do processo de impeachment contra Santiago Peña . Na sessão conjunta do Congresso, porém, foi colocada em votação o pedido de renúncia do presidente.

A oposição defendia que o Congresso rejeitasse a renúncia e desse continuidade ao impeachment . Os parlamentares argumentavam que a saída voluntária permitiria a Peña assumir uma vaga de senador vitalício, com direito a foro privilegiado.

➡️ No Paraguai , ex-presidentes que concluíram seus mandatos ou renunciaram ao cargo ganham o título de senador vitalício, o que lhe garante imunidade parlamentar pelo restante da vida.

O senador de oposição Líder Amarilla alegou que aceitar a renúncia poderia impedir que o presidente respondesse a eventuais acusações na Justiça.

"Se aceitarmos esta renúncia, o que estamos fazendo é permitir que Santiago Peña obtenha foro parlamentar e que todo o dinheiro que foi roubado fique impune, porque a Promotoria não poderá apresentar acusações contra ele", disse Amarilla, em entrevista ao ABC Color.

Já os governistas sustentavam que aceitar a saída do presidente seria a maneira mais rápida de encerrar a crise política e permitir a transferência de poder ao vice-presidente, Pedro Alliana.

O grupo também afirmava que o Senado poderia analisar um eventual pedido de retirada do foro de Peña, caso a Promotoria solicitasse a medida.

Segundo Ariel Palacios, comentarista da GloboNews e especialista em América Latina, Peña tentou se blindar e manter seu foro privilegiado ao anunciar sua decisão de renunciar. Isso porque, pela Constituição do Paraguai , ao deixar o cargo, os ex-presidentes da República viram senadores vitalícios.

A manobra, no entanto, foi frustrada quando a Câmara deu seguimento à abertura do impeachment. A Carta constitucional estabelece que o ex-presidente perde essa prerrogativa se tiver sido submetido a julgamento político e for considerado culpado.

Opositores advertiram que aceitar a renúncia permitiria a Peña ter uma blindagem parlamentar, impedindo que fosse julgado pela Justiça comum pelas suspeitas de crimes relacionados à crise do banco ueno.

👉 A Constituição paraguaia estabelece que é prerrogativa do Congresso aceitar ou rejeitar a renúncia do presidente da República e a do vice-presidente.

Santiago Penã apresentou sua carta de renúncia em um vídeo , em que se desculpou com a população que perdeu o acesso ao próprio dinheiro e disse que decidiu renunciar "pensando na estabilidade do nosso país, na paz social e na necessidade de preservar nossas instituições democráticas".

"Estou convencido de que nenhum cargo pode estar acima do bem-estar do Paraguai . Também quero pedir desculpas ao povo. Se em algum momento falhei, nunca foi minha intenção decepcionar a confiança que depositaram em mim", disse.

➡️ Santiago Peña é alvo de críticas por conta da crise bancária que começou após o banco digital ueno fechar as portas e deixar milhares de clientes sem acesso ao próprio dinheiro . Peña foi acionista do grupo que controla a instituição, e a oposição acusa o Banco Central paraguaio de encobrir irregularidades ( leia mais abaixo ).

Santiago Peña, economista e ex-ministro da Fazenda durante o governo de Cartes, é o atual candidato presidencial do Colorado — Foto: REUTERS

Clientes do banco ueno fazem protesto em Assunção, no Paraguai, em 5 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Daniel Duarte/ AFP

“Nunca antes alguém prejudicou, em um único dia, 3 milhões de pessoas na República do Paraguai , e o senhor conseguiu isso, senhor presidente... o senhor é a origem desse monstro que criou”, disse a deputada de oposição Rocío Vallejo durante a sessão, pouco antes da apresentação do pedido.

A acusação foi apresentada por 35 deputados, que pediram ao presidente da Câmara a convocação da sessão extraordinária.

Penã foi acionista do grupo dono do banco

Deputado da oposição no Paraguai segura cartaz em ato que pede impeachment do presidente Santiago Peña após fechamento de banco virtual que gerou crise bancária no país, em 5 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Cesar Olmedo/ Reuters

👉 Peña, que também é economista, foi acionista do grupo proprietário do ueno até março do ano passado . O banco tinha cerca de 3 milhões de clientes e concentrava aproximadamente US$ 850 milhões em depósitos públicos, incluindo recursos do Instituto de Previdência Social.

O ueno, que pertence ao Grupo Vázquez, fechou as portas na terça-feira (3), depois que o Banco Central iniciou sua liquidação. A autoridade monetária identificou uma insuficiência de recursos para cobrir as obrigações do banco, relacionada a empréstimos concedidos a empresas vinculadas à instituição.

Em uma publicação em suas redes sociais, o presidente paraguaio afirmou que os responsáveis pelas irregularidades responderão à Justiça , sem exceções. A declaração foi feita pouco antes de que ele promulgasse uma lei que permitirá aos clientes do ueno recuperar seu dinheiro mais rapidamente.

“Peço veementemente a todos os setores políticos que coloquem o interesse dos poupadores acima de qualquer outro interesse”, afirmou.

Executivos do ueno se entregaram às autoridades após a emissão de mandados de prisão pela Procuradoria, que também acusou formalmente 27 pessoas ligadas ao banco. A Justiça ordenou ainda o bloqueio dos bens dos acusados.

Nesta quarta-feira, também circularam relatos de falhas em aplicativos de outros bancos, o que aumentou a preocupação com o sistema financeiro do país.

A Associação de Bancos do Paraguai (Asoban) informou que as instituições financeiras trabalhavam para atender ao grande volume de clientes que estavam transferindo suas contas do ueno. A entidade ressaltou que o sistema bancário continuava “operando normalmente”.

Pessoas fazem fila para tentar retirar dinheiro em banco em Assunção, no Paraguai, diante de temor gerado por crise bancária no país, em 3 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Daniel Duarte/ AFP

articles.title: Enem 2026 Piauí: mulheres e pardos são maioria dos inscritos | G1
articles.standfirst: No Piauí, 120,8 mil candidatos se inscreveram para o exame, sendo 72,1 mil mulheres e 48,7 mil homens.
articles.summary: O Enem 2026 no Piauí registra 120,8 mil inscritos, com maioria feminina e de autodeclarados pardos; confira o perfil dos candidatos e como ver o local de prova.
articles.body:
Enem 2026: o que pode e o que não pode levar para o exame? Veja lista e regras do dia de prova — Foto: Reprodução

As mulheres representam a maioria dos inscritos no Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) 2026 no Piauí. Dos cerca de 120,8 mil participantes registrados no estado, 72,1 mil são do sexo feminino, enquanto 48,7 mil são homens.

Os dados mostram ainda que a maioria dos inscritos se autodeclarou parda, com 71.802 participantes. Em seguida aparecem pessoas brancas, com 27.171 inscrições, e pretas, com 16.316.

O levantamento registra também 3.296 inscritos sem declaração de cor ou raça, 1.692 pessoas amarelas e 527 indígenas. As informações estão disponíveis no Painel Enem 2026, do Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (Inep).

O perfil escolar mostra que 46.347 participantes estão cursando a última série do ensino médio. Desse total, cerca de 42 mil são estudantes da rede pública que tiveram a inscrição realizada automaticamente. Outros 40.129 já concluíram essa etapa da educação básica.

Há ainda 32.522 inscritos que estão cursando o ensino médio, mas não devem concluir essa etapa em 2026, além de 1.806 que não estão estudando nem concluíram o ensino médio.

Enem 2026: locais de prova já podem ser consultados

Os locais de aplicação do Enem 2026 já estão disponíveis para consulta no cartão de confirmação de inscrição, na Página do Participante.

Para acessar o documento, o candidato deve entrar no endereço enem.inep.gov.br/participante e fazer login com os dados da conta Gov.br (CPF e senha).

O cartão de confirmação informa o endereço do local de prova, o idioma escolhido para a prova de língua estrangeira (inglês ou espanhol), as datas do exame e eventuais solicitações de atendimento especializado e tratamento pelo nome social.

Após consultar o documento, a recomendação é pesquisar o endereço do local de prova, verificar a distância e o tempo de deslocamento e, se possível, simular o trajeto em um domingo.

Os portões serão abertos às 12h e fechados pontualmente às 13h. A orientação é chegar com antecedência para evitar atrasos.

O exame será aplicado nos dias 8 e 15 de novembro, dois domingos consecutivos.

45 questões de Linguagens, sendo 40 de Língua Portuguesa e cinco de língua estrangeira (inglês ou espanhol);

Os candidatos devem ficar atentos aos itens permitidos para a realização do exame. Confira:

Documento oficial de identificação com foto. Documentos digitais também são aceitos, desde que apresentados nos aplicativos oficiais;

Caneta esferográfica de tinta preta, fabricada em material transparente;

Cartão de confirmação de inscrição (não é obrigatório, mas é recomendado);

Lanche e água em garrafa transparente, sem rótulo. Os alimentos poderão ser vistoriados pelos fiscais.

Entre os documentos digitais aceitos estão:

Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (CNH) Digital;

O candidato deve apresentar o documento diretamente no aplicativo oficial. Capturas de tela não serão aceitas. Após entrar na sala de aplicação, o uso do celular continua proibido.

19h: término da aplicação no primeiro dia;

18h30: término da aplicação no segundo dia.

O candidato só poderá sair do local de prova levando o caderno de questões nos últimos 30 minutos que antecedem o encerramento do exame.

Como a prova tem duração de até cinco horas e meia, também é recomendado usar roupas e calçados confortáveis.

articles.title: Rio Branco registra menos chuva que o previsto para outubro | G1
articles.standfirst: Capital registrou 77,2 milímetros de chuva no mês, enquanto a previsão era de 150 mm. Defesa Civil alerta que precipitações irregulares não são suficientes para elevar o nível do manancial.
articles.summary: Capital registrou 77,2 milímetros de chuva no mês, enquanto a previsão era de 150 mm. Precipitações irregulares não são suficientes para elevar o nível do manancial.
articles.body:
Rio Branco registrou 77,2 milímetros de chuva em outubro, pouco mais da metade dos 150 mm previstos para o mês . Segundo a Defesa Civil Municipal, o volume representa 51,5% do previsto . Em novembro, a expectativa é de 206,2 mm de precipitação.

Conforme o órgão, a falta de chuvas regulares também tem dificultado a recuperação do Rio Acre, que marcou 1,75 metro na medição das 5h desta quinta-feira (5), na capital.

Ao g1 , o coordenador da Defesa Civil de Rio Branco, tenente-coronel Cláudio Falcão, explicou que as chuvas têm ocorrido no estado de forma irregular e que o manancial segue baixo dos dois metros em um período em que já deveria apresentar elevação.

“Já era para a gente estar com o nível do Rio Acre bem mais elevado e não estamos. [...] Isso porque não temos chuvas regulares que possam contribuir o suficiente para elevar o nível do manancial. E quando essa chuva acontece, o sol está tão intenso que essa água não escoa, ela não chega dentro do rio, não chega nos igarapés, nas represas”, afirmou.

Os dados de outubro ajudam a entender esse cenário. Na primeira quinzena do mês , Rio Branco registrou apenas 27,66 milímetros de chuva, o equivalente a 18,4% dos 150 mm previstos para todo o período, segundo levantamento da Defesa Civil Municipal.

Rio Branco registrou 58,86 mm de chuva até o dia 18 de outubro — Foto: Arquivo/Defesa Civil de Rio Branco

Até o dia 18, o acumulado chegou a 58,86 mm, ou 39,2% do esperado. A maior concentração ocorreu em 16 de outubro, quando choveu 31,2 mm. Na ocasião, a precipitação provocou alagamentos em ruas da capital.

Mesmo com esse episódio de chuva mais intensa, o volume acumulado não foi suficiente para alcançar a previsão mensal.

Ainda segundo Falcão, a recuperação do Rio Acre agora depende de precipitações frequentes, capazes de manter o volume de água nos rios e igarapés. A previsão, porém, é de que a estiagem continue até o fim do ano , em razão da influência do fenômeno El Niño.

Conforme a Defesa Civil, a situação preocupa porque o Rio Acre está a 52 centímetros da menor marca histórica registrada em Rio Branco para o período, de 1,23 metro, em 2024.

Falcão informou também que a menor cota registrada pelo manancial neste ano foi de 1,58 metro e que, atualmente, o rio apresenta a terceira pior marca dos últimos 11 anos , segundo a Defesa Civil. O coordenador também alertou que uma nova redução pode agravar o cenário.

''É possível que, se não vierem chuvas nesse período agora, a gente decresça e se aproxime da marca de 2024. Aliás, nós já estamos próximos. Caso o nível fique abaixo de 1,50 metro, a situação hídrica na capital pode se tornar ainda mais complicada”, destacou.

Rio Branco termina outubro com volume de chuvas quase 50% abaixo do esperado, diz Defesa Civil — Foto: Victor Lebre/g1

O cenário de outubro contrasta com o registrado em setembro, quando Rio Branco teve um volume de chuvas acima do esperado para o mês, mesmo durante o período de estiagem.

Na ocasião, foram registrados 168,6 mm de chuva, enquanto a previsão era de 92,7 mm. O volume ficou 81,9% acima do esperado. Apesar disso, o Rio Acre continuou em nível baixo.

A Defesa Civil explicou, na época, que as chuvas trouxeram impactos positivos, principalmente para a zona rural, mas não foram suficientes para resolver os efeitos da estiagem.

Por isso, a recuperação do manancial depende da continuidade das precipitações nos meses seguintes.

articles.title: Pena de morte na Califórnia: Newsom substitui penas de 548 presos | G1
articles.standfirst: Estado da Califórnia tem um quarto de todas as penas de morte nos Estados Unido. Medida é uma das últimas de Gavin Newsom antes de deixar o cargo.
articles.summary: A pena de morte na Califórnia foi comutada para 548 detentos por decisão de Gavin Newsom, que considerou a prática incompatível com os valores morais do estado.
articles.body:
Gavin Newsom, governador da Califórnia e possível candidato democrata à presidência dos EUA. — Foto: Mike Blake/Reuters/Arquivo

O governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newsom, em um de seus últimos atos no cargo, substituiu as penas de todos os presos condenados à morte no estado para prisão perpétua, sem possibilidade de liberdade condicional.

São 548 detentos no total. Essas condenações representam cerca de um quarto de todas as penas de morte nos Estados Unidos .

A medida foi divulgada em uma carta aberta nesta quinta-feira (5). No documento, Newsom escreve que, como governador, concluiu que, sob a perspectiva moral, o estado da Califórnia não pode matar os detentos.

"Tomo esta medida porque acredito firmemente que a morte sancionada pelo Estado é incompatível com os valores da Califórnia, mina os alicerces do nosso sistema jurídico e diminui cada um de nós", escreveu.

"Podemos agora deixar esses criminosos morrerem no anonimato, enquanto lembramos e honramos para sempre as suas vítimas".

De acordo com o jornal "The New York Times", a Califórnia tem mais condenados a pena de morte do que qualquer outro estado dos EUA.

Sala de execução da pena de morte no Alabama — Foto: AP Photo/Dave Martin, File

A ação é um dos últimos atos do governador porque ele deve deixar o cargo em dois meses com o intuito de se preparar para a disputa presidencial dos Estados Unidos. As próximas eleições do país acontecem em 7 de novembro de 2028.

"Esta decisão está entre as mais difíceis da minha carreira, não porque eu duvide de sua necessidade para o nosso estado, mas porque sei que seu anúncio pode trazer à tona lembranças excruciantes para as famílias das vítimas. Respeito profundamente a opinião daqueles que discordarão com veemência da minha decisão, inclusive algumas famílias de vítimas que sofreram a pior perda possível", continuou Newsom.

A Constituição da Califórnia determina a revisão, pela Suprema Corte do estado, do pedido do governador para reduzir as penas.

"Embora eu confie que este ato de clemência categórica seja compatível com a lei da Califórnia, reconheço que minha decisão de exercer minha autoridade constitucional de clemência exige que os juízes participem de uma decisão de grande peso que não escolheram assumir e com a qual podem discordar pessoalmente", pontuou o governador.

Não há previsão de quanto tempo os pedidos de revisão irão demandar.

Em dezembro de 2024, o então presidente Joe Biden tomou a mesma medida : anulou a pena de morte para 37 condenados. Os réus passaram a cumprir prisão perpétua sem direito a fiança. Na época, Biden disse que condena os assassinos, mas que estava convencido de que o país não deve ter pena de morte a nível federal.

articles.title: She thought her Hinge match’s photo looked off. Then she realized why
articles.summary: Dating apps have an AI problem. More users say they’re seeing increasingly hard-to-detect fake photos.
articles.body:
A young woman was scrolling through Hinge when she noticed something appeared slightly off with Johnno, a young man she matched with.

When she asked him if his photos were AI, he replied, "Hahaha appreciate it nah no AI here."

But a reverse image search showed otherwise, revealing Johnno, or whoever was posing as him, had used AI to deepfake his face onto photos of other men from Pinterest.

When the woman shared her experience in a TikTok that racked up 1.2 million views, something even weirder happened in the comment section. Women posted screenshots of profiles from Andy, Roger and Ben, each with different facial features and hair, but sporting the same flannel shirt and linen pants Johnno was wearing, against the same beachfront background.

"Me realizing the guy I was talking to was using AI pics from this post…," one user commented. "I came across a guy that did this too!! Every single photo came up on a photo search from Pinterest," one woman commented. "It's a breeding ground for catfish and it's just gonna get worse so buckle up," another user commented.

These increasingly subtle, hard-to-detect modifications are an issue dating experts say is becoming more common as users navigate a barrage of artificial intelligence in the dating world, from AI-aided prompts and conversations to increasingly sophisticated photo edits.

Amy Chan , a dating coach and the author of " UNSINGLE: How to Date Smarter and Create Love That Lasts ," says her clients have encountered an increase of AI-altered images and conversations.

AI is rapidly changing the online dating world for young people, as more than half of adults under 30 report using dating apps like Tinder, Match, Bumble and Hinge, according to 2023 data from Pew Research .

2026 data from Match and the Kinsey Institute finds that nearly four in 10 U.S. singles have used AI in their dating lives. The trend is especially pertinent in young users, with 67% of Gen Z singles reporting using AI.

A crop of new apps like Your Move AI, FireTexts, Keys AI and Rizz function as AI wingmen, analyzing conversations and providing options on how to respond. And AI-native dating apps like Amata, Known, Sitch and Ditto are using artificial intelligence as the basis of their matchmaking technology.

In other viral videos , women recounted similar experiences with profiles like Johnno.

"This might be one of the most disturbing things I've ever seen on a dating app," content creator Dana Kuritzkes says at the start of the video about the experience of a friend who matched with a man using AI-generated photos on Hinge in the Bay Area. "Her first thought, and I quote, was, 'Why do all of these photos look like stock images?'"

In the video, she scrolls through screenshots of the profile, examining staged photos of a hike and one at a winery where people's fingers are missing from the glasses.

Online dating coach Austin Dunham recounted that a friend sent him screenshots of a Hinge user who cloned a photo of him from Instagram in a white shirt against a palm tree.

"The fact that women are catching on to this and can spot where things are coming from goes to show how many guys are actually starting to use AI photos," Dunham explained in a Sept. 17 TikTok . "I believe it's going to cause a really big epidemic in terms of the online dating space," Dunham said.

Chan says there's nothing wrong with using AI for some grammatical help editing a bio. But using AI to essentially create a personality, or alter the one you have to be more interesting, is an issue.

While suitors may think they're coming across as more intelligent or funny by using AI to come up with their bio and prompts, Chan warns it may have the opposite effect.

"Someone can read it, detect the AI copy and not be interested in engaging with you further," Chan says. "Authenticity is a value people crave more than ever, (and) using washed down, AI answers is the antithesis of that."

Dating apps know they have an AI photo problem. More are instituting live verification

Brandon Wade, founder and co-CEO of Seeking.com , says the platform has seen a proliferation of AI, with some individuals registering accounts under multiple phone numbers and testing out alternate profiles to compare results.

"People have realized hey it's a numbers game," Wade says. "With the use of AI they can now run multiple dating profiles on multiple different sites to be able to get the results that they want."

Wade warns that these AI profiles can also be tied to scammers who target vulnerable individuals who are looking for companionship or professionals with disposable income.

The platform in January 2025 introduced a Selfie Liveness Check to verify a live selfie against uploaded profile photos. Data from 2025 found the new feature caught 53,000 scammers on the platform, many of who were posing as entirely generated users of different races, ages and genders. Seeking.com found that a majority of these scammers were coming from romance scam hotspots in Africa and Southeast Asia.

"We do see more of that sort of activity specifically from scammers because they are trying to cast a much broader net and target people that way. With actual genuine daters, that is not a behavior that we're seeing as often," Wade says.

Tinder and Bumble also started requiring similar biometric face checks for U.S. users.

Hinge offers optional AI-enabled features to help users improve their prompts. They employ a combination of AI-based moderation tools and human moderators to vet profiles. In March 2026, they started rolling out Face Check, a verification process that uses a selfie video to confirm a person's authenticity and that their face matches their profile.

"The authenticity of our community is important to helping daters find safe and meaningful connections," Ben Celebicic, Hinge's chief product and technology officer, told USA TODAY. "If a user decides to include generative AI on their profile, it should not be used to misrepresent themselves or their intentions. Our goal is to ensure that our users only leverage AI to build trustworthy connections with other daters, so they can find love and delete the app."

The issue with these verification processes, commenters online point out, is that many instances of AI do use someone's real face, bypassing verification processes, but later edit subtle elements of a photo to make their attire, physique or background more interesting. These apps also face privacy concerns from users about how facial verification videos and photos are collected are stored.

Chan says it's the digital equivalent to lying, and that the same goes for over-filtering a photo. Men in the comments have pointed out that they've also encountered AI-fueled photos on women's profiles, as well as heavily edited ones.

"I have had clients who show me their profile, and I'm like, 'that doesn't look like you.' They get defensive and I have to tell them matter of factly, the photo has been so altered, or it's a very old photo that they've altered, that they're setting themselves up for a bad date," Chan says.

Instead, she advises clients to keep their profiles realistic and true to themselves. She recommends exchanging a few messages and going straight to either a video chat or IRL.

Otherwise, users risk going right back to square one.

"The person will feel shocked and deceived and that is usually impossible to bounce back from on a first date," Chan says.

articles.title: An American man with shifting identities and grandiose movie plans is convicted of murdering his girlfriend and child in Rome
articles.summary: An Italian court found American Rexal Ford guilty of double murder in a bizarre and disturbing case that has gripped the nation. He plans to appeal.
articles.body: “My name is Rexal Ford,” the man born under the name Charles Francis Kaufmann told an Italian courtroom, in English, at the start of his double-murder trial in February. “I am not a killer. I am a film producer.” The former Kaufmann, a 47-year-old American, did legally change his name to Rexal Ford in 2019. In Malta, in 2022, however, he was known as Daniel R. Foster, with a British passport and Maltese residency papers to match. Three years later, hiring a boat from Malta to Sicily, he had an Italian identity document identifying him as Matteo Capozzi — a name that also appeared with his photo on a now-deleted IMDb page claiming production credits on major film projects. “You’re going to get caught up on names of convenience?” Ford asked me, when I raised the subject of his multiple passports. “You’re saying you never pretended to be someone you aren’t? Even once?” On Thursday, in Rome’s Court d’Assise, Ford was convicted of double homicide and concealment of a corpse for, according to the prosecution, killing his 28-year-old partner, Anastasia Trofimova, and their 11-month-old daughter, and dumping their bodies in a public park. Judge Paola Roja read the verdict without comment, sentencing Ford to life in prison with three years of solitary confinement. Ford’s lawyer said that he expected the verdict to be appealed, a standard practice in Italy where even small crimes are afforded two appellate trials. Behind the verdict lay a long-running, sensational case of gruesome mystery, tall tales and shifting identities, at the junction of con artistry and the film business — of a man who wined and dined would-be investors and producers in Rome’s finest restaurants while he and his family lived in the streets and slept in the park. Across multiple interviews before and during his trial, in Rome’s Rebibbia Prison and Santo Spirito Hospital psychiatric ward, Ford maintained that he was not the person who committed the killings. “I had nothing to do with it,” he told me, in his easy California accent, when we first met in the prison visiting room in October 2025. Other claims of his were not so consistent. When we spoke in May, in the psychiatric ward during a pause in his murder trial, Ford claimed to be “John Montgomery from England.” He also told me that he was a spy and that other people in the room were clones. The court had allowed him to be hospitalized for what it called a “brief psychiatric condition,” then brought him back after a court-appointed consultant deemed he had improved and was likely “faking psychosis.” Before the murders, in 2023, Ford managed to convince the Italian Film Board to offer him nearly $1 million for a fake movie project, according to the ministry of culture, in a scandal that led to the resignation of a government official. A disturbing discovery and national call for clues On June 7, 2026, a child playing on a jungle gym in Rome’s Villa Doria Pamphili park saw what she thought was a doll under the bushes. It was the body of a baby. Her nanny raised the alarm and police were called. Within an hour of searching the park, the city’s largest, police had found the body of a woman as well, this one in an advanced state of decomposition, leaving her unrecognizable. She had blond hair and the authorities were able to identify four distinct tattoos: a skeleton with a surfboard on her outer right arm, intertwining bird wings on her inner right arm, an ornate floral garland with hanging stars on her abdomen, and a winged red design on her inner right foot. Autopsies revealed that the two were mother and daughter, and that they had died on different days, the woman around June 4 or 5 and the child late on June 6, the day before they were discovered. The causes of death, the authorities reported, were suffocation and strangulation that had left no broken bones and no bruises or marks. The child had not been fed for perhaps days before she was killed, but she had no other injuries, prosecutors told the court during the trial. The two remained nameless for more than a week. Finally, after an Italian missing-persons TV program, “Chi L’ha Visto,” aired images of the tattoos, someone called in to say that they recognized the ankle tattoo. It belonged to a woman the caller had often seen with a man and a baby in Campo de’ Fiori in central Rome. Not long after, another member of the public sent the program a snapshot of that same family. In it, the man was bleeding from his temple, after what the caller alleged was a drunken fight. The woman, she said, had appeared to be trying to comfort the man while holding the baby. More people called in, declaring that they had seen the couple in a Starbucks, at a local vegetable market, and in the park where they sometimes slept. The media reported, and prosecutors confirmed during the trial, that police had encountered the man twice between June 5 and 6, while he was acting drunk and erratic and carrying the still-living baby. In both instances, police said they had let the man go after he flashed his American passport and film credentials. Asked about the incidents, a spokesperson for Rome’s police said they routinely stop “drunk Americans” and let them go. The spokesperson said, and testified in court, that Ford had told the officers his wife was sleeping in their hotel room. Giuseppe Cascini, the chief prosecutor in the case, said that the police involved in the encounters had been sanctioned for their failure to intervene. Police had also received a phone call late on the night of June 6 from a 16-year-old boy who said he’d seen a man carrying a “limp baby” on the street by Villa Doria Pamphili, near a place where there is a breach in the park wall. The police did not dispatch a car to check, in part because the teen admitted he had been out at a club all evening, vice prosecutor Antonio Verdi said in his closing arguments. An arrest in Greece Ford said in an interview that he had not seen any of the media coverage after the bodies were discovered. “I don’t speak Italian and I don’t watch Italian news,” he said. Had he known about the deaths at all? “How would I?” he said. “She took the baby and left me for an old boyfriend who was rich.” On June 11, CCTV cameras captured him leaving the Campo de’ Fiori area with a large dark rolling suitcase, which investigators never found. Using his Rexal Ford passport, he flew to the Greek island of Skiathos, famous as the backdrop of the film “Mamma Mia.” Police say they tracked his passport and cell phone to locate him, with the help of the FBI, and he was arrested under a warrant from Interpol. He did not fight extradition, according to the lawyer who was representing him at the time, and was brought back to Italy on June 13, when his name and various aliases were released to the public. Rome’s public prosecutor would eventually announce the names of the dead on June 18. Ford denied any involvement in the killings, and he accused the Italian investigators of being “mafiosi” who were out to get him, according to evidence given by the lead prosecutor in his trial. After “Chi L’ha Visto” had run a few episodes on the murders, a Russian woman from Siberia contacted the program, saying she was Anastasia Trofimova’s mother. The producers flew her to Rome, where she told them that she and her husband had lost touch with their daughter in Malta, but that she knew Trofimova had had a baby with a “rich American film producer.” One of the show’s producers said in an interview that the woman didn’t have photos of her daughter to share, and she couldn’t offer much in the way of detail about her life. Through an interpreter, she said that her daughter had lost all of her documents when her backpack fell into the sea on the family’s trip from Malta to Italy in 2025. The self-identified parents were unable to produce enough documentation to repatriate their daughter’s body to Siberia. They stopped communicating with the Italian authorities, said Arturo Salerni, the lawyer representing the victims’ interests, and they were unavailable to return to Rome or to testify during the murder trial. During closing arguments at the trial, Verdi did show a grainy phone video of Trofimova holding the baby, which he said had been sent by Trofimova’s parents. In it, Trofimova is speaking English as the baby squirms in her lap. Mother and child both remain frozen in a Roman morgue, unclaimed, the coroner said at the end of the trial. Making movies from Malta Ford said he met Trofimova in Maltia, in the fishing village of Marsaskala, in 2022. “We hooked up and hung out and then she disappeared for about a year,” he said. “Then she showed up on my doorstep and I regret ever letting her in.” A dark-haired waitress who goes by Ana at the St. Thomas Bay bar in the village could confirm that the couple had been there, Ford said. A waitress matching this description at the bar, who would not give her last name when approached, said she had been friends with Ford and Trofimova, who everyone had known as Stella. Ford used a credit card in the name of Daniel R. Foster, she said, but everyone called him Rexal or Rex, and she had assumed that was what the middle initial R. stood for. Ford’s landlord in Marsaskala, who asked not to be named due to concerns over the possible negative impact on his rental business, said he had registered under the Foster name, and had paid his rent six months at a time. Ford said that while he was in Malta, he was working on a film called “Food Fight: The Great Culinary Battle of Malta.” The movie was listed on IMDb and then removed, but still appears in other databases, which describe the subject as “two ruthless rivals who come head-to-head in this intense battle of culinary supremacy of the Mediterranean.” It was never released. Also during his time in Malta, he said, he applied to the Italian Ministry of Culture for a filmmaking grant for a project called “Stelle della Notte,” to be produced by his own company, Tintagel Films, in conjunction with the Italian production firm Coevolutions. The application was submitted in 2020, and after the film board’s internal vetting process, the grant was awarded in 2023. In Rome, Ford would entertain potential backers of “Stelle della Notte” with lavish meals, promising them a star-studded production shot at premium — and pricey — locations including the Piazza Navona, Castel Sant’Angelo and some of the Eternal City’s best terraces, according to three different people who took part in the meetings. He boasted of jetting between Japan, New Zealand, England and Hawaii to finalize various film projects; a document obtained by Italian television and presented in court claimed that Harrison Ford was on the budget as lead, for $4 million, with Kevin Spacey at $600,000 as a fallback option. Chef Gordon Ramsey would play himself, according to the bogus grant application. Marco Perotti, the executive producer of Coevolutions, insisted in an affidavit entered into evidence that the film for which he’d co-signed the grant application was genuine, but said he had no idea he was “working with an assassin.” Perotti did not respond to requests for comment, but he continues to produce films with Italian and international producers. A secretive crossing The couple’s child was born at home on June 14, 2024, delivered by a Russian midwife named Rita, according to Ford. Reached in person in Malta, Rita confirmed that she had delivered the child, but couldn’t remember the exact date. Ford said he contacted the US Embassy in Malta to register the child, but there are no records of a foreign birth abroad to an American on the date he said she was born. Prosecutors told the court in Rome that the child had no legal birth certificate, and that Ford, as her sole living parent, is the only person who could arrange for her body to be repatriated. Trofimova, Ford claimed, had been working as a computer hacker for a Russian crime syndicate when they met. He described a hotel in Marsaskala where she had allegedly worked with a group laundering money for the syndicate. An anti-mafia investigator in Malta said in an interview that the hotel and Trofimova, who was living in Malta under a different identity, had both been under investigation in a hacking inquiry. The investigation into Trofimova was dropped after her death, according to the investigator. When I visited the hotel in question, a low-rise cement structure with an internal courtyard swimming pool and rundown ‘80s decor, a Russian-speaking guard stopped me from entering the second floor, saying the rooms were rented out “for an event.” Outside the building were an assortment of generators, cables and Starlink dishes. Ford claimed that he and Trofimova had started siphoning funds from the people she worked for, and their theft was discovered. Between that trouble and the baby’s lack of papers, he said, they needed to escape Malta anonymously, via private boat. “We had to leave without being followed,” he said. Italian investigators said that Giovanni Costagliola, a boat service operator in Malta’s capital, Valletta, told them Ford had contacted him by text message, under the name Matteo Capozzi, seeking passage for his “wife and infant” and asking if they needed documentation. After he told Ford that insurance did require the documents, Costagliola testified in court, “He never contacted me again.” According to a re-creation of their movements during the murder trial, the family did arrive at Ragusa, on a private yacht in March of 2025. The skipper who transferred them testified that the woman and baby were silent on the 90-minute trip. From Sicily, the family traveled by train to Rome, where Ford got in touch with a fantasy book author he had been seeking to make a deal with, Federico Carro. He told Carro he was working to get financing to buy the rights to one of his novels. Carro told RAI public television that Ford said he had been scouting locations in Malta, New Zealand and then Iceland. Carro said Ford had also told him that he was the son of the rock star Lita Ford, of the Runaways. On April 5, Carro met Ford, Trofimova and the baby, who was introduced to him as Sara. They spoke several more times about various projects, but then Ford told Carro he had gone back to England. On June 5, Ford left a final voice message on Carro’s phone, which was entered into evidence in the murder trial. In it, Ford asked if he and the baby could stay at Carro’s house for a few nights. “I’m back in Rome now, just me and my child,” Ford said. The baby’s mother, he said, had left him for a wealthy old boyfriend. An ‘unorthodox approach’ After Ford was returned to Rome and charged with double homicide, Nicola Borrelli, the General Director of Cinema and Audiovisual at the Italian Ministry of Culture, stepped down and the ministry issued an apology to Italian taxpayers for having made the film grant. The Italian film board launched an investigation into how the grant had been approved. Among the lines of inquiry was whether Trofimova had used her hacking skills to falsify some of the background information that made Ford’s Tintagel Films look like a legitimate company. A lawyer for Borrelli declined to comment on whether the investigation had found anything to support that speculation. In our interviews, Ford often bragged about films he had previously made including one called “Story: The Movie,” in 2008. In a video on YouTube, Ford – Kaufmann at the time – is seen being interviewed at the premier as the movie’s director. In the video, he appears young and confident, telling his interviewer, “I’m excited for my first time out … I lucked out with the cast because you know I actually went through sort of an unorthodox approach.” Ford was not present for the verdict. His lawyer said that his client had refused to meet with him since June, and that when Ford returns to court for an appeal, “it won’t be me next time.” The prosecutor Verdi, addressing the media after the verdict, called Ford “cold, calculating, manipulative, and a pathological narcissist.” “He possesses a strong, distinct personality,” Verdi said, “but he is an imposter whose game is up.”

articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed puts hands on Sky News reporter in hostile confrontation hours before election victory
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed confronted a Sky News reporter, dismissing the British journalist's questions just hours before winning Michigan's Senate race.
articles.body: Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, had a viral, combative exchange with Sky News reporter James Matthews just hours before his Senate victory Tuesday, even putting his hands on the journalist. "Are you registered to vote in the state of Michigan?" El-Sayed asked as he walked up to reporter James Matthews. "I'm not," the British correspondent, who is based in the U.S., responded. "Why would I care to have a conversation with you?" the Democrat fired back. EL-SAYED MOCKS TRUMP, VANCE AND ROGERS IN GLOATING VICTORY SPEECH SIGNALING COMBATIVE TONE IN SENATE After Matthews said he was a journalist, El-Sayed scoffed and replied, "in the U.K." "You know how many votes I want to get in the U.K.? Zero," El-Sayed told Matthews as he placed both hands on the reporter's shoulders. "I'm never running for office in the U.K." Matthews stressed that the 2026 midterms "matters to the world" and told El-Sayed he was "bidding to be a senator." DEMS SEIZE THE SENATE AS BLUE TIDAL WAVE CRASHES DEEP INTO TRUMP COUNTRY, TOPPLES GOP STRONGHOLDS "A senator in where? What country? What country?" El-Sayed retorted while placing his hands on Matthews' shoulders again. "The United States," Matthews answered. "What country are you with?" El-Sayed then asked. "I'm based in the United States," Matthews said. "But you report for where? Where are your viewers?" El-Sayed interrupted. El-Sayed dismissed Matthews when claiming Sky News viewers were international, insisting "Sky News is not viewed in the United States of America," then sneering that "like five people" watch the network in the U.S. "I've answered all the questions, I've answered all the questions for the viewers of the United Kingdom. So I'm going to ask you to stop chasing me around. Please," El-Sayed said before walking away. Matthews denied to El-Sayed he was "chasing" him around. MICHIGAN VOTERS MAKE SURPRISING CROSS-PARTY CHOICES AS ROGERS, EL-SAYED RACE REACHES FINAL HOURS According to Sky News, Matthews "repeatedly sought an interview" with El-Sayed. The Democrat had another tense exchange with Matthews on Monday as he attempted to press him about the defection of Democratic Michigan Rep. Haley Stevens, who had endorsed GOP rival Mike Rogers. "If you keep being in my way, I'm not going to be very happy," El-Sayed told the reporter. Sky News issued a statement in support of its reporter. "We’re proud of our correspondent James Matthews, who was doing his job: covering the election campaign and asking straightforward questions on behalf of our audiences," a Sky News spokesman told Fox News Digital. "The outcome of U.S. elections has ramifications globally, including in the U.K. and across the 138 countries worldwide where millions of people consume Sky News." The El-Sayed campaign didn't respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment. El-Sayed, who has had multiple tense exchanges with reporters in the run-up to the midterms, defeated Rogers in the closely watched Senate race for a seat Republicans were hoping to flip this election cycle. articles.title: Major tech stocks plunge as US midterms sparks fears of AI slowdown
articles.summary: The market has been reacting to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the AI industry following the US midterms
articles.body:
Hundreds of billions of dollars in market value has been wiped from major tech firms in a stock market rout after the US midterm elections sparked concerns of a slowdown in AI development.

Following Democratic wins after election campaigns run on slowing AI, shares in firms across the tech and artificial intelligence sectors plummeted.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite stock index closed down by more than 5.5% to lose an estimated $2.5tn in market capitalisation, according to Dow Jones data, while other key US stock indexes also saw big losses in their worst days since 2025.

The sell-off comes on top of broader concerns about whether the huge amounts being spent on AI will pay off.

Democrats in races across the US campaigned to slow the onslaught of data centres and AI, and there were dozens of measures on ballots around the country aimed at restricting the development of the hubs crucial for powering the technology.

Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned heavily against data centres, pledging a moratorium on new construction in the sector.

Shares in companies heavily exposed to AI data centres, including crucial chipmakers and semiconductor manufacturers, fell sharply on Thursday, highlighting investor concerns that had already been growing.

Nvidia shares slid more than 9%, knocking more than $400bn off the firm's market value.

Other chipmakers also suffered, with AMD and Micron both dropping by more than 17%. Intel shares also dropped, down 10.3%, while memory card maker SanDisk plunged more than 22%.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which tracks the performance of 30 of the largest companies involved in semiconductor production, fell by more than 12%.

Shares in Elon Musk's companies SpaceX and Tesla also plunged, falling 8% and nearly 11% respectively and shaving more than $300bn off the firms' market value on Thursday.

Musk had spent nearly $450m backing Republican campaigns, including at least $45m in support of Ken Paxton for the Texas senate seat, but Texas was turned blue in the Democratic tsunami on Tuesday night.

In total, the so-called magnificent seven tech companies, including Apple, Nvidia and Tesla, have shed a trillion dollars in value in a single trading day.

The stock falls also hit other major US stock indexes. The S&P 500 index fell by 4.4% by the end of trading, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average erased gains made on Wednesday to close down more than 3.4%.

The Nasdaq Composite fall was so large it is now in what market watchers call correction territory, which is where an index or company value falls at least 10% below its recent high.

Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, said the steep sell-off on the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 was sending shockwaves into other markets.

"Fresh panic over the AI trade has hit Wall Street hard," she said.

"Fears that the vast sums poured into AI infrastructure may not deliver the returns investors have been banking on are now colliding with the prospect of a sharp slowdown in data centre construction."

Some tech leaders have said they were caught off guard by the backlash against data centres in the midterms.

OpenAI president and co-founder Greg Brockman said he believed everyone had been surprised by the reaction to data centres, and more work needed to be done to ensure communities were on board.

"A lot of our shift over the course of this year has really been to realise that from San Francisco trying to build infrastructure in Texas, Georgia, and other places, you can't just tweet and say: 'This is going to be good.' You need to be in those communities," Brockman said at the WSJ Tech conference in Napa, California on Wednesday evening.

Meta's president Dina Powell McCormick said that the industry needed to put more effort into selling AI as a good idea.

"I think we need to double and triple down on telling the story," she told the WSJ conference.

Alongside the immediate impacts of the US mid-term elections, some investors have become concerned that AI shares could be in a bubble that is due a correction .

articles.title: Farage says he is worried Trump will step up Iran war after midterm 'disaster'
articles.summary: Donald Trump "broke a promise" to the American electorate by launching the war, Reform UK leader adds.
articles.body:
Nigel Farage has said he fears Donald Trump will "aggressively" continue his war with Iran after his "disaster" in the US midterm elections.

The Reform UK leader said the US president was still a friend, but accused him of having "broke a promise" to the American electorate by launching the war.

The war in Iran, which the US began in February 2026, weighed heavily in the midterm election results earlier this week in which the Democrats swept Trump's Republicans out of power in Congress.

Farage, who had initially urged people to support the war, said that following the election results he worried Trump would respond with more strikes on Iran.

Asked how he thinks President Trump will respond, Farage told broadcasters on Thursday: "I suppose I worry that the president will continue aggressively attacking Iran.

"That worries me because that would have even more serious implications for the price of oil, for inflation, for the whole western world".

He acknowledged he had initially supported the war but stressed he "never supported endless war".

Asked if the war was a mistake, he said: "There's no question about it."

The US president had "always kept his promises," added Farage, but "in this case, he said no more foreign wars and here we are in month eight of a war with no sign of ending."

"That and the resulting fuel prices are what in the end has done the damage."

Trump said on Tuesday that the poor results for Republican congressional candidates were partly due to the war and the related surge in oil prices.

But he insisted he did not regret launching a joint attack with Israel on Iran.

In recent weeks, Trump has warned the US and Israel could return to all-out war after the midterms if a deal to end the conflict cannot be reached with Iran.

There have been various warnings , including from politicians in the UK, that Trump may now step up his attacks on Iran but Farage's criticism was more vocal than many have been.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier this week he hoped the midterm results meant there was an "opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all, and that's the cost of living".

Farage said he had not spoken to Trump since the midterms but described it as a "complete wipeout" and "an absolute shellacking" for the Republicans.

Trump's loss limits powers at home, but it will likely be different abroad

'This is a disaster': Angry Republicans blame Trump for midterms defeat

"Trump has had an amazing career - he has beaten the pollsters, he has gone way beyond expectations," he added.

"This was his last big election and they all say, that all political careers end in failure."

His comments came at an event to announce Reform's first defence spokesperson, after the party was criticised for not having one.

Angus MacIntyre said he had stood down from a 40-year military career, including as a Wing Commander in the Royal Air Force (RAF), to take on the role.

MacIntyre pledged in a speech to end prosecutions of serving military personnel and veterans within the first 100 days of a Reform government.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting and Tory leader Kemi Badenoch had criticised Reform for lacking a defence spokesperson despite having dedicated posts for immigration, the economy and education.

Farage said MacIntyre would form part of "a team we will build to represent us" on the issues of defence, security and cybersecurity.

articles.body: Ukraine on Thursday said it expected the outcome of the US midterm elections to create new opportunities for support from Washington, after the victory of Democrats in both US houses.Speaking at a press conference in Bucharest, foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said Kyiv was hopeful that the political changes in the United States would lead to further assistance."We expect new dynamics. Every change always gives a chance for new dynamics. We expect new steps to support Ukraine," he said, Reuters reported.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had also welcomed the Democrats' gains a day earlier, expressing hope that their projected takeover of both chambers of Congress from January would result in greater military and financial assistance to Kyiv.In an interview with German broadcaster ZDF on Wednesday, Zelenskyy said Democrats had been vocal in their support for Ukraine, while also calling for closer ties between Washington and European countries."I am also grateful to the Republicans, but the Democrats speak very clearly about supporting Ukraine and providing assistance to Ukraine," he said."They speak about renewing the connection between the United States and Europe... Therefore, there is hope that a balance of power will emerge and that we will receive more support," Zelenskyy added.Trump has largely halted direct financial and military assistance to Ukraine, despite support for US aid among lawmakers from both parties.Zelenskyy said stronger American financial and military backing could also increase pressure on Russian President Vladimir Putin."If Congress now speaks of strong financial support or military assistance, as Europe is doing and demonstrating today, then that will be something positive that will have an impact on Putin."Democrats' congressional gains could open path for Ukraine aidThe Democrats' victories in the midterm elections could give them greater influence over legislative priorities, including efforts to provide assistance to Ukraine, Reuters reported.The election results followed public anger over Trump's policies, particularly the impact of the US-Iran war on the cost of living. Democrats secured at least 54 seats in the Senate against the Republicans' 44, after winning contests in traditionally Republican states. They also gained at least 28 seats in the House of Representatives.With control of both chambers of Congress from January, Democrats will be able to determine which legislation comes up for a vote and when. New aid for Kyiv could secure the necessary two-thirds majority to overcome a veto by US President Donald Trump, according to Reuters. Democratic aides have identified assistance to Ukraine as a priority.The outcome sets the stage for a possible legislative deadlock in Washington over the next two years. It will also mark the first time Trump, who previously served as president from 2017 to 2021, faces a Congress in which Democrats control both chambers.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A 63-year-old woman smears faeces in her husband's mouth after threatening to make him eat it at £1 million farmhouse; handed 12-month suspended jail term; judge calls attack ‘gratuitous degradation’
articles.summary: A 63-year-old woman in the UK has been handed a suspended prison sentence after smearing her own faeces into her husband's mouth during a violent
articles.body: A 63-year-old woman in the UK has been handed a suspended prison sentence after smearing her own faeces into her husband's mouth during a violent confrontation at their £1 million farmhouse in the New Forest. Alison Moore subjected her husband, Rob Moore, to several assaults over an extended period before carrying out the disturbing attack at their home in Damerham. The incident was heard at Southampton Crown Court, where the judge described the act as a 'gratuitous degradation' of the victim.According to reports by the Daily Mail, The Sun and Daily Star, Moore was sentenced to 12 months in prison, suspended for 18 months. She had previously pleaded guilty to three counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm.Prosecutor Andrew Coley told Southampton Crown Court that the attack took place on August 20, 2026, following an argument between the couple. Moore pushed her husband onto their bed at their farmhouse after accusing him of failing to stand up for her during an earlier pub visit. She also reportedly called him 'boring'.During the confrontation, Moore told her husband, "You talk so much s**t, I'm going to make you eat it," before following through on the threat by smearing her excrement into his mouth.Mr Moore managed to break free and went to wash his mouth and change his clothes. Before cleaning himself, he took a photograph showing his face smeared with faeces. The image was subsequently presented to the court as evidence of the assault.Police were called to the property, following which Moore was arrested. She initially made no comment during her police interview and later submitted a written statement that the prosecution described as a 'bare denial'.The Daily Mail and The Sun reported that the incident was part of a longer pattern of violence against her husband, rather than an isolated confrontation.Husband suffered earlier assaults, court hearsThe court also heard details of previous attacks in which Moore had allegedly struck her husband on the back with a broom handle and hit him in the face while wearing a wedding ring.Photographs taken following incidents in March 2024 and August 2026 showed a cut above Mr Moore's eye, along with an injury and redness on his back.The prosecution also outlined the events leading up to the August attack. Three days after the broom-related incident, the couple had spent an afternoon at a pub, where they argued about when to leave. They subsequently stopped at another pub, but staff reportedly refused to serve Moore before the couple returned home.Moore allegedly blamed her husband for not standing up for her during the incident. Prosecutor Andrew Coley described the subsequent attack as premeditated, citing the ongoing resentment between the couple.Defence cites depression, bereavements and relationship problemsRepresenting Moore, defence barrister Rose Burns told the court that her client deeply regretted her actions and accepted full responsibility for the assaults.However, she argued that Moore's behaviour was partly driven by what she perceived as an imbalance in the relationship. The defence also highlighted the emotional difficulties she had experienced following a series of family bereavements.The court heard that Moore had lost both her parents in 2024 and 2025. Her sister had also died earlier in 2026 after suffering a head injury in a fall down a staircase. She had additionally experienced the deaths of an uncle and her dog.Burns said these circumstances had contributed to a deep depression, leaving Moore feeling trapped and frustrated with her life.The defence also told the court that Moore had sought private mental healthcare at the Priory to review her relationship with alcohol. Financial disagreements had reportedly added to the tensions between the couple, with Moore wanting to sell their farmhouse while her husband opposed the idea.Burns said her client was determined to change her behaviour and hoped that reconciliation with her husband might still be possible.However, she acknowledged that no amount of poor behaviour by Mr Moore could justify the violence inflicted upon him.Judge calls the attack a ‘gratuitous degradation’Judge Gary Lucie acknowledged the personal difficulties Moore had experienced but made it clear that her circumstances did not excuse her actions.Referring specifically to the use of faeces during the assault, he said, "The use of faeces was a gratuitous degradation of the victim."He also observed that the impact of the offences on Mr Moore was evident, despite his decision not to have his victim impact statement read aloud in court.The judge further raised concerns about Moore's relationship with alcohol, telling her that she did not appear to have fully accepted its role in her offending.Mr Moore had asked the court not to impose a restraining order against his wife. He attended the sentencing hearing and, despite the ordeal, left the courthouse alongside her.Moore's previous convictions and assault caseThe case also brought attention to Moore's previous convictions, which include driving with excess alcohol, assault by beating and using violence to secure entry to a property.These offences related to an incident on April 6, 2022, when Moore reportedly turned up at the home of a builder with whom she was infatuated and attacked his partner on the doorstep, pulling out a clump of her hair.Although she initially denied the charges, she was subsequently found guilty at Southampton Magistrates' Court.She received a 12-month restraining order and was prohibited from entering a street in Damerham for a year. She was also ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid community work, undertake rehabilitation activities and pay £500 in compensation to the assault victim, along with £715 in court costs.Moore had spent three weeks on remand at HMP Bronzefield before her latest sentencing and is understood to be living in an Airbnb in Dorset.You use AI every day.
