Fox News Digital reached out to the Redmond Fire Department for comment.

articles.title: An Oregon college student was held at knifepoint by his brother. He escaped, and police shot him.
articles.summary: Maverick Lyon, a college lacrosse player, filed a federal civil rights case alleging excessive force and negligence on the part of the city of Albany and Benton County.
articles.body: A college athlete in Oregon who was shot multiple times by police while he was escaping a dangerous encounter with his brother alleges excessive force and negligence in a federal civil rights case filed Wednesday. Maverick Lyon, a college lacrosse player, was home in Albany on Jan. 6 when his brother, who had relapsed into drug use, held him at knifepoint, attorneys with Stritmatter Law said in the suit. Their father called Albany police after he saw the altercation on a security video in the family’s home. Lyon grabbed another knife in self-defense during the encounter and managed to escape through the back door, the lawsuit says. According to the suit, after Lyon dropped the knife, police shot him at least five times. His injuries led to four weeks in the hospital and serious operations. The lawsuit says Lyon was shot even though he followed police commands. Benton County said in response to an NBC News request that it does not comment on pending litigation. The city of Albany, which is also named as a defendant, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Lyon’s attorneys said in a statement that after the shooting, surgeons “removed half of his right lung, his spleen, his appendix, and performed extensive reconstructive surgery on his digestive system.” His parents, David and Laura Lyon, said in a statement: “I have always believed that when you call 911, help is coming. I never imagined that making that call would leave me wondering if my son was going to survive.” “Our family has been through something no family should ever have to experience. I called the police that day because I wanted to protect Maverick, and instead, the very people I called for help ended up nearly taking his life,” they said. According to the lawsuit, the family’s ordeal began after Jan. 5, when David and Laura Lyon told a Benton County probation officer that their elder son, Dakota, was “acting dangerously toward family members” and had relapsed into using drugs. They asked the county to take Dakota Lyon into custody, but it declined to, according to the lawsuit. “The next day, David called 911 after Dakota’s drug-induced behavior escalated to taking their youngest son, Maverick Lyon, hostage at knifepoint inside the home,” the lawsuit says. Albany police surrounded the Lyon house, where officers could identify Maverick and Dakota through a window, according to the lawsuit. Maverick was mouthing “help me” to the officers through the window, it says. It also alleges that police were familiar with Dakota Lyon and knew Maverick was the victim in the incident. Police told Maverick to come outside and drop a knife he had grabbed in self-defense, but “when Maverick did as instructed, Albany Police officers shot Maverick at least five times in the chest, back, and face after he had dropped the knife, came outside, and presented no threat,” the lawsuit says. It says that rather than provide Maverick with medical assistance, police “yelled at Maverick to roll over and submit to handcuffing while Maverick was on the ground bleeding.” The Albany Police Department said in a statement at the time that its officers were involved in a shooting after they responded to a domestic disturbance and encountered a person with a knife. Two officers fired their weapons, striking the person who had the knife, it said, adding that the officers “immediately rendered medical aid until emergency personnel arrived.” Dakota Lyon was later sentenced to more than six years for the incident with his brother. According to KVAL-TV of Eugene, he acknowledged his responsibility in the case, and his attorney said Lyon wished he could have taken the bullets instead of his brother. The lawsuit alleges excessive force, battery, negligence and violation of Maverick Lyon’s Fourth Amendment rights. It seeks a jury trial and damages. Benton County District Attorney Ryan S. Joslin previously ruled that the shooting was justified. Joslin said that after an investigation, he determined that the officers’ decision to “fire their duty weapons in this case was based on an objectively reasonable belief that to do so was necessary in order to protect their own lives or the lives of fellow officers.” The decision “must be made in light of what the officers knew and perceived leading up to and at the exact time their decision was made,” he said. “In this case, the officers, in real time, had only fractions of a second to decide how to act.” The district attorney’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. David and Laura Lyon said they support their son’s lawsuit. “We cannot change what happened that day, but we want answers, accountability, and changes that help prevent another family from experiencing the pain ours has,” they said in their statement. “Most importantly, we want Maverick to have every opportunity to heal, move forward, and live the life he deserves.”

articles.title: Tourist hot spot faces housing revolt as locals demand cuts to vacation lodging
articles.summary: Mallorca, Spain, welcomed 13.5 million visitors in 2025, and now a business leader says the popular island must curb tourism and cut vacation rental capacity.
articles.body: One of Spain's most popular vacation islands is facing calls for a limit on tourist accommodations to curb crowding. Jordi Mora, president of Pimem, a federation representing small and medium-sized businesses in Mallorca, said the island needs to take stronger steps to control tourism, according to the Majorca Daily Bulletin. "We need to curb tourism, which includes reducing the total number of tourist beds," Mora told the outlet. POPULAR DESTINATION CRACKS DOWN HARD ON TOURISTS AS NEW LIMITS THREATEN SUMMER GETAWAYS Mallorca, one of the Balearic Islands, received some 13.5 million visitors in 2025, a significant number for an island measuring roughly 1,400 square miles, Fox News Digital previously reported. Mora's proposal would include reducing the number of accommodations available in registered vacation rentals and taking stronger action against illegal rentals, the Majorca Daily Bulletin reported. Fox News Digital reached out to Pimem for comment. Mora said some smaller hotel operators would support reducing accommodations if the changes were made through agreements and incentives. "If this is approached through consensus and incentives, it is possible to move toward a more sustainable model," Mora said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER A travel expert previously discussed the issues faced by the Balearic Island with Fox News Digital. "Once a place goes viral, it can get flooded with visitors really quickly. It’s great that people want to explore new places, but those places aren’t always set up to handle that kind of attention," travel expert Jordi Lippe-McGraw said. Mallorca's large visitor numbers have also brought other tourism concerns into focus. "That’s when you start to see overcrowding, higher costs for locals and more pressure on the area overall." Mallorca has also been exploring a shift toward attracting fewer visitors who spend more money. Pedro Homar, managing director of Palma's tourism board, said Mallorca would prefer to attract wealthy American tourists, Fox News Digital reported. "Tourism is our way of life," Homar told The Wall Street Journal. "The change of model is quality over quantity. We need to have fewer tourists who spend more." American tourists in Spain spent about $410 per day this past July, compared with $240 for German visitors and $260 for British travelers, according to The Wall Street Journal. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES Mora also said the island does not need more tourists to grow its economy. "We must increase value and ensure that this growth benefits society as a whole," he told the Majorca Daily Bulletin. The clash with residents is especially noticeable in Mallorca, where thousands took to the streets in June 2025 to protest the growth of tourism on the island, Fox News Digital reported at the time. Demonstrators marched with signs saying, "One more tourist, one less resident." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Mallorca's large visitor numbers have also brought other tourism concerns into focus. Viral videos over the summer appeared to show pickpockets targeting tourists near Palma, including older visitors near popular attractions, Fox News Digital previously reported. Travel expert Angel Castellanos told Fox News Digital at the time that crowded tourist areas can create opportunities for thieves, particularly when visitors are distracted or unfamiliar with their surroundings. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "The takeaway isn't to avoid these places," Castellanos said. "It's to travel smarter." Andrea Margolis of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.
